newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finnish forestry sees no clear upturn before Feb.
newsitem.headline: Finnish forestry sees no clear upturn before Feb.

text.p: The Federation of Finnish Forest Industries' new chairman Juha Niemela said on Wednesday he expected no clear signs of an upturn before February.
Niemela is also CEO of UPM-Kymmene, Europe's biggest forest industry group.
"Most probably we won't see very good signs before, say, February," Niemela told Reuters after a news conference at the federation's autumn meeting.
His remarks came after the federation issued a report headlined "Upturn ahead" which said an increase in European growth was expected but that prospects were still uncertain.

"In the normal case the paper industry starts to live strongly again in February," Niemela said, but added that the outlook was still uncertain and that prospects for the Finnish industry hinged on trends in Finland's key trading partners.
"The forecasters betrayed us this year," he said. "They forecast about double the growth that is now materialising. Again there are ... good forecasts, but let's hope this time that they are right."
"We cannot determine better than the experts," Niemela said referring to the general economic outlook. He also declined to predict price trends for forest industry products.
